description:
What happens if you smoke weed every day for 10 years? At first, daily cannabis use can feel harmless. It helps you relax, sleep, and shut off stress. But tolerance can build within weeks.

Over time, frequent THC exposure can affect motivation, memory, decision-making, sleep, and emotional regulation. Some daily users develop Cannabis Use Disorder, while chronic smoking can also lead to coughing, airway inflammation, and other respiratory problems. Research has also linked frequent cannabis use with higher odds of heart attack and stroke. The good news is that some effects may improve after quitting. CB1 receptors can recover, cognitive performance may rebound, and respiratory symptoms can ease.

But after a decade of daily use, recovery doesn’t necessarily happen overnight.

description:
History has seen periods like this before. Massive government debt, stressed banks, falling trust in institutions, political division, and market instability are all hitting at the same time.

According to the Strauss–Howe generational theory, that may not be a coincidence. The theory argues that societies move through roughly 80-to-100-year cycles, ending in a period of crisis known as the Fourth Turning. Previous cycles have been associated with events like the American Revolution, Civil War, and World War II. Now rising debt costs, commercial real estate problems, generational wealth gaps, and declining institutional trust are creating another dangerous mix.

History doesn’t guarantee what happens next, but if the pattern holds, we may already be living through the most unstable part of the cycle.
